subject: Insurance
title: Age and Gender Pricing
description: A micro-lesson that makes Age and Gender Pricing usable.

hook.text: A 16-year-old male pays $6,000+ a year for auto insurance. A 40-year-old woman pays $1,500.

buildup.text: Teen drivers are 3x more likely to crash than adults.

discovery.text: Rates drop sharply at 25 when accident rates decline. By 40, premiums stabilize.

twist.text: Six US states have banned gender-based pricing.

climax.text: Age and gender pricing is actuarially sound but socially contested.

quiz.question: Why do young male drivers pay the most for auto insurance?
options: They have statistically the highest crash rates
